sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word of a verse ("sulfur and ___"). Nothing earlier tells the baker what fell, so the answer can't be reasoned out, only guessed from wording they haven't seen.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the last word of a phrase ("a pillar of ___"). No earlier card gives the baker a way to reason it out, so it is a guess at wording.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: This story card retells verse 5 ("Send them out to us..."), which is exactly the right answer the baker just gave on card 6. The answer is used again on a later card.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
